description: PLOS ONE research article. Methylation profiling of tumor suppressor gene (TSGs) promoters is quickly becoming a powerful diagnostic tool for the early detection, prognosis, and even prediction of clinical response to treatment. Few studies address this in salivary gland tumors (SGTs); hence the promoter m
title: Quantitative Methylation Profiles for Multiple Tumor Suppressor Gene Promoters in Salivary Gland Tumors
Resilience and Recovery in the Informal Economy: Social Networks, Social Protection, and Adaptive Strategies Among Post‐COVID Workers in Bangladesh
creator: Md. Abdullah Al Mamun, Khandakar Farid Uddin, Md. Shawan Uddin, A. N. M. Jahangir Kabir, Md. Nazirul Islam Sarker
description: The informal economy is vital in developing countries by providing income opportunities to marginalized populations. The COVID‐19 pandemic intensified existing vulnerabilities, causing severe income loss and heightened insecurity. The study aims to investigate the impact of COVID‐19 on informal workers’ income and livelihoods, explore their adaptation strategies, and assess the role of social networks and social protection in enhancing resilience.

title: Exercise type, dose and mental health outcomes in youth: Which types and doses are sufficient?
creator: Huagen Wang, Yisheng Aku, Shicun Xu, Zhanbing Ren, Yingjie Zhang, Runsen Chen, Jing An
description: BackgroundAlthough experimental evidence supports links between exercise and certain mental health indicators, epidemiological research has focused primarily on the dose–response effect of a single type of exercise, overlooking potential differences across exercise types in their associations with overall and specific mental health outcomes.

title: Endoparasites of Rattus norvegicus With Reference to Their Zoonotic Importance in an Urban District, East Kuwait
creator: Fatemah A M Aryan, Laila Mohammed Azad Tahrani, Osama Mohammed El-Shafei El-Azazy, Valeria Pasciu
description: Rattus norvegicus (the brown rat) is adaptable to living in urban settlements across the globe, including Kuwait where this rodent species is widespread in human habitats. It has been known that brown rats are reservoirs of many pathogens, including parasites that can pose a threat to human and animal health.

title: What makes serious illness conversations acceptable? A mixed-methods study of patient and caregiver experiences in oncology and cardiology
creator: Alston Ng, Su-Min Yeo, Shirlyn Hui-Shan Neo
description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to identify how contextual, dispositional, and relational factors intersect to shape the participant experience of serious illness conversations (SICs) while exploring the nuances of appraisal across different clinical specialties.MethodsA convergent parallel mixed-methods study was conducted as part of a Serious Illness Care Programme pilot at two Singaporean tertiary centres.

title: Shade Avoidance Restricts Soybean Breeding Progress and Increases Herbivore Susceptibility
creator: Lukas Vonmetz, Emanuel B. Kopp, Simon Jäggi, Pascal A. Niklaus, Samuel E. Wuest
description: High planting densities expose field crops to competition for light, which typically induces shade avoidance responses such as stem elongation. While adaptive in natural environments, these responses can lower yield and increase susceptibility to stress in agricultural systems. We tested whether soybean breeding over the past century has altered shade avoidance and associated trade‐offs.

title: Association Between Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction and Subsequent Detection of Sick Sinus Syndrome and Atrial Fibrillation in Patients With Unexplained Syncope
creator: Hironobu Sumiyoshi, Hidemori Hayashi, Akira Nakashima, Toshikazu Kono, Maki Ono, Akira Mizukami, Tohru Minamino
description: BackgroundAtrial fibrillation (AF) and sick sinus syndrome (SSS) frequently coexist and may share common atrial structural and electrophysiological remodeling substrates. Left ventricular (LV) diastolic dysfunction frequently coexists with AF; however, its association with subsequent detection of SSS and AF remains incompletely understood. This study investigated whether LV diastolic dysfunction is associated with the detection of SSS and AF.

title: Mitigating plume surface interactions using lunar craters
creator: Seamus L Anderson, Prabal Saxena, Philip T Metzger
description: Launching and landing spacecraft on the lunar surface mobilizes regolith at high velocities which will likely cause damage to nearby objects and infrastructure, a phenomenon known as plume surface interactions (PSIs) that must be mitigated for sustainable lunar surface exploration.

title: Sodium Nitrate Combined With Dental Pulp Stem Cells Alleviates Atherosclerosis Through Inhibiting Oxidative Stress
creator: Zhuang Mao, Han Duan, Zhichao He, Lin Lv, Haichao Yu, Hu Cao, Jingyuan Shao, Xuesong Zhang, Shunying Hu, Hua Wang
description: Atherosclerosis (AS), a leading cause of cardiovascular disease (CVD), is closely associated with excessive oxidative stress. Dietary nitrate has emerged as a promising intervention for cardiovascular protection through the nitrate–nitrite–nitric oxide (NO) pathway. Meanwhile, dental pulp stem cell (DPSC) possess potent antioxidant properties. However, the potential synergistic effect of sodium nitrate (NaNO3) and DPSC on AS remains unclear.

title: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) NAD/Sirtuin Deficiency and SARM1-Mediated Synaptic Vulnerability: Evidence for Accelerated Brain Aging Subtypes
creator: Ngo Cheung
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Anxiety disorders and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) often occur alongside signs of accelerated biological aging, yet the molecular pathways that connect genetic liability to synaptic and circuit-level dysfunction remain unclear. We performed a multi-gene-set transcriptome-wide association study using large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for anxiety disorders and PTSD, with a focus on curated aging-related pathways across brain regions involved in fear, reward, memory, and stress regulation.The analysis identified 185 significant enrichments, with strong cross-disorder concordance in senescence, telomere maintenance, and

title: Facial Recognition Analyses Reveal Social Networks of Co‐Occurrence at Harbor Seal Haul‐Out Sites
creator: Wyatt Hall, Abigail Hanson, Sydney Dunn, Ava Benton, C. Filipowicz, Ahmad Khazaee, Tolga Dinçer, Krista K. Ingram
description: Understanding the behavior and population dynamics of harbor seals ( Phoca vitulina ), an ecologically significant and widespread coastal pinniped, is vital to effectively manage vulnerable coastal marine ecosystems. A novel, non‐invasive facial recognition technology was used to identify harbor seals at haul‐out sites across two consecutive molting seasons in Middle Bay, Maine.

title: Evaluating the Use of a Commercial Bacterial Biomass as a Bioactive Component of Pacific White Shrimp Litopenaeus vannamei Feeds
creator: Magida Tabbara, Adela Araujo, Sidra Nazeer, Silvio Peixoto, Richard Smullen, Matthew Briggs, D. Allen Davis
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Survival, growth rate, and welfare have always been the primary concerns of shrimp aquaculturists. Accordingly, a number of bioactive feed components have been supplemented in shrimp feed to improve health condition, feed intake, and growth. The present study evaluated the effects of supplementing a high ash, low protein marine bacterial biomass on feeding behavior, growth, proximate composition, hemolymph biochemistry, and digestive enzyme gene expression of juvenile Litopenaeus vannamei.

title: Prevalence, Genetic Diversity, and Risk Factors of Cryptosporidium spp. in HIV/AIDS Patients: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis (2017–2025)
creator: Farzad Mahdavi, Mohammad Reza Mohammadi, Shayan Heidari, Roumina Norouzi, Ali Pouryousef, Kambiz Karimi, Asma Mousivand, Mahtab Mehboodi, Ali Asghari, Hassan Nourmohammadi
description: Background Cryptosporidium spp. is a major opportunistic pathogens in HIV/AIDS patients, contributing substantially to morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite advances in HIV/AIDS management, the global burden, genetic diversity, and risk factors of cryptosporidiosis in this high‐risk group remain incompletely understood.

title: irAE.AI: AI-powered exploration of real-world immune-related adverse events
creator: Gabriela Fort, David Stone, Ching-Nung Lin, Arabella Young, Aik Choon Tan
description: ObjectivesImmune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer treatment, but their clinical benefit is limited by the onset of immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Real-world pharmacovigilance data, such as the FDA’s Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database, offer the scale needed to better characterize and understand these toxicities.

title: Treatment outcomes of daptomycin- and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium bloodstream infection
creator: Wei-Ting Lin, Jia-Ling Yang, Chi-Ying Lin, Sung-Hsi Huang, Yu-Chung Chuang, Jann-Tay Wang, Yee-Chun Chen, Shan-Chwen Chang
description: ObjectivesAmong patients with daptomycin-resistant and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium bloodstream infection (BSI), the optimal definitive therapy is uncertain. We estimated the dose effect of daptomycin (≥11 mg/kg versus 8 to <11 mg/kg) on 28-day mortality and exploratorily described outcomes in patients treated with linezolid.MethodsAdults with VRE BSI who received linezolid or daptomycin ≥8 mg/kg were included.

title: Homozygous TFR2 (c.2093_2096del) Mutation in an Asymptomatic Patient With Type 3 Hereditary Hemochromatosis, First Report From Saudi Arabia
creator: Omar M. Raslan, Dana S. Alamoudi
description: Hereditary hemochromatosis (HH) is an inherited disorder of iron metabolism characterized by progressive iron accumulation in multiple organs. While most cases are associated with HFE mutations, non‐HFE variants such as mutations in the transferrin receptor‐2 (TFR2) gene represent rare causes of iron overload.

title: Cervical Skip Metastases and Extensive Central Venous Thrombosis as the Initial Presentation of High‐Grade Prostate Adenocarcinoma With Discordant PI‐RADS 3 Findings: A Case Report and Diagnostic Challenge
creator: Yuchun Luo, Benhui Lai, Juncheng Huang
description: Prostate cancer can initially present with cervical lymph node “skip” metastases and extensive central venous thrombosis, without pelvic or bone involvement. A PI‐RADS 3 lesion on mpMRI does not exclude high‐grade (Gleason 5 + 5 = 10) disease. Unexplained thrombosis in elderly men warrants prostate cancer investigation.

title: Retraction: Anti-neuroinflammatory and neuroprotective potential of Cissus tuberosa ethanol extract in Parkinson’s disease model through the modulation of neuroinflammatory markers
creator: The
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In Tables 6 and 7, the reported values for the standard error of the mean appear unusually repetitive. title: Primary Petit's Triangle Hernia With Bowel Strangulation: Management in a Resource‐Limited Setting
creator: Biruk Umer Mohammed, Henok Bahru Wodajeneh, Ashenafi Tesfaye Bedada, Frewoyni Gedey Gebregziabher, Dereje Nigatu Elala
description: Lumbar hernias are rare surgical entities that may present asymptomatically or with complications such as obstruction and strangulation. We report a case of a 45‐year‐old woman who presented to the emergency department with a painful, irreducible swelling in the right lumbar region accompanied by vomiting, abdominal pain, and obstipation.

title: Plasma proteomic signatures of subclinical atherosclerosis progression for cardiovascular risk stratification: A cohort study
creator: Yani Huang, Ruixin Gao, Jianxin Li, Bin Yang, Keyong Huang, Shufeng Chen, Jie Cao, Xiaoqing Liu, Chong Shen, Ling Yu, Liancheng Zhao, Ying Li, Dongsheng Hu, Jianfeng Huang, Bin Lu, Dongfeng Gu, Fangchao Liu, Xiangfeng Lu, Suzanne De Bruijn, Suzanne De Bruijn, Suzanne De Bruijn, Suzanne De Bruijn
description: BackgroundExisting risk stratification tools inadequately identify individuals with subclinical atherosclerosis (SA) who could benefit from early intervention. This study aimed to develop protein risk scores (ProtRSs) for SA progression and assess their incremental value for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk prediction.

title: ClC-7 links PIKfyve inhibition to Rab-dependent LRRK2 activity at lysosomes
creator: Devin Clegg, Amanda Bentley-DeSousa, Agnes Roczniak-Ferguson, Shawn M. Ferguson
description: Clegg et al. show that LRRK2 integrates distinct lysosomal stress signals through stimulus-specific combinations of interactions with Rab GTPases and GABARAP. PIKfyve inhibition activates LRRK2 through ClC-7–dependent accumulation of a subset of Rabs on lysosomes without requiring GABARAP, whereas CASM-inducing stresses require both Rab and GABARAP interactions.

title: Material Hardship Among Affluent and Poor Households in the United States
creator: John Iceland, Jaehoon Cho
description: We examined the correlates of hardship among affluent households and the characteristics of affluent households make them less likely to report hardships than poor ones. Is it income alone that explains differences in the likelihood of hardship, or do other characteristics—such as wealth and education—play important roles?

title: The AMPK kinase Sak1 activates separase and promotes its nuclear localization during mitosis
creator: David Vaquero-Pelaz, José-Antonio Rodriguez-Rodriguez, Malina Carmina Ilinca, Esther Casas-Fernández, Amparo Picard, Francisco Del Caño-Ochoa, Isabel Vernia, Toni Gabaldón, Maria Angeles Juanes, Ethel Queralt
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Vaquero-Pelaz D et al. show that the kinase Sak1 activates separase, promoting its nuclear accumulation and mitotic function. A hypermorphic SAK1-E50K allele boosts separase activity, while human LKB1 associates with separase, revealing a conserved kinase-protease regulatory axis. Introduction

Sister chromatids are held together before mitosis by two key mechanisms: DNA catenation, which involves the intertwining of their DNA strands, and cohesin complexes, specialized protein structures that physically link the chromatids.

title: Incidence, Prevalence and Diagnostic Delay in Pyoderma Gangrenosum: A Finnish Nationwide Registry-based Study
creator: Suvi-Päivikki Sinikumpu, Jari Jokelainen, Laura Huilaja
description: stimated global prevalence 0.018% (3). Although some studies suggest that PG diagnoses may have increased slightly in recent years (4), data remain limited. As PG ulcers are painful and the disease associated with a high risk of comorbidities (2), prompt diagnostic evaluation is essential. We therefore aimed to study the incidence trends, prevalence and diagnostic delay of PG.

title: Safety and Effectiveness of Embolization via the Ophthalmic Artery with N-butyl Cyanoacrylate for Anterior Skull Base Meningiomas
creator: Takeru HIRATA, Satoshi KOIZUMI, Hideaki ONO, Satoru MIYAWAKI, Shigeta FUJITANI, Motoyuki UMEKAWA, Nobuhito SAITO
description: Anterior skull base meningiomas are often supplied by ethmoidal arteries branching from the ophthalmic artery. Preoperative embolization can reduce intraoperative bleeding and facilitate safer resection; however, its use is limited by the risk of visual complications. This study evaluates the safety, effectiveness, and technical considerations of embolization via the ophthalmic artery using n-butyl-2-cyanoacrylate (n-BCA).

title: Asymmetric metaphyseal cones versus medial modular block augment with central cone for medial tibial defects
creator: Yi Ren, Chloe E. H. Scott, Nick D. Clement, Shuqiao Xie, Pankaj Pankaj
description: AimsManaging large medial tibial bone defects during total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains technically demanding, particularly in elderly patients. This study quantitatively compares two reconstructive strategies: ‘bridging’ the defect using an asymmetric metaphyseal cone versus ‘anatomical reconstruction’ employing a symmetrical cone with a metallic block augment, and assesses their sensitivity to osteoporotic bone quality.

title: Real-World Safety of Fluticasone Furoate/Umeclidinium/Vilanterol in Patients with Asthma or Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), and Clinical Outcomes in COPD: Post-marketing Surveillance in Korea
creator: Eun-Bin Lee, Jung-Eun Cho, Eunsun Kwon, Karam Ko, Sang Heon Kim, Sang-Ha Kim
description: Background Fluticasone furoate/umeclidinium/vilanterol (FF/UMEC/VI) is a single-inhaler triple therapy administered via the ELLIPTA inhaler (GSK). FF/UMEC/VI 100/62.5/25 μg was approved in Korea to treat chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in 2018 and asthma in 2022 (100/62.5/25 and 200/62.5/25 μg). Safety and efficacy of FF/UMEC/VI are well established in global clinical trials, though Korean real-world evidence remains limited.

title: Low-dose histrelin for ovulation induction in mares: a partially randomized crossover pilot study
creator: Lys de Barros Fogagnoli, Kallena Canali Abdala Jose, Rachel Weckl, Clara Mantovani Ozorio Mota, Mirelle Ochrimowicz Fernandes, Rafaela Caroline Machado, Carlos Eduardo Camargo, Pedro Vicente Michelotto
description: This partially randomized crossover pilot study evaluated reduced doses of histrelin for ovulation induction in mares and compared intramuscular (IM) administration with pharmacopuncture at the Bai-hui and Yan-chi acupoints. Eleven mares were enrolled, of which nine completed all eight protocols and were included in the analyses.

title: Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy and Elite-Level Sports
creator: Quirina Thio, Juliette van Hattum, Francisca Nijland, Maarten Moen, Arthur Wilde, Harald Jørstad
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundApical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (aHCM) is a distinct, rarer phenotype with a potentially more favorable prognosis and lower morbidity than nonapical forms of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, yet its specific interaction with elite-level sports remains poorly defined.Case SummaryThis case describes an asymptomatic athlete found to have aHCM, for whom engaging in elite sports from ages 17 to 31 years did not lead to adverse morphologic changes or progression of apical fibrosis or disease, even after the cessation of his professional sports career.DiscussionThis case underscores the

title: A GA3-loaded hydrophilic–lipophilic diblock polymer acts as a nano-safener to alleviate herbicide-induced injury in rice by activating key metabolic pathways
creator: Xile Deng, Heng Qiao, Yijie Zhan, Jie Shen, Lianyang Bai, Shuo Yan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Although herbicides are among the most effective tools for weed control in rice cultivation, they often cause phytotoxicity. Herbicide safeners can mitigate such damage; however, commercial safeners may have adverse effects on non-target organisms. Natural safeners such as gibberellin A3 (GA3) are considered safer alternatives, but new strategies are needed to improve the utilization efficiency of GA3 because its poor solubility and limited potency restrict its practical application.

title: Blind Estimation Versus Direct Measurement of the Arterial Input Function in Dynamic Contrast‐Enhanced MRI of the Breast
creator: Jake L Cray, Jiří Vitouš, Radovan Jiřík, Sofya Titarenko, David L Buckley
description: PurposeAccurate arterial input functions (AIFs) are essential for quantitative dynamic contrast‐enhanced (DCE) MRI, yet direct measurement is challenging and population‐averaged AIFs neglect patient‐specific variability. Blind deconvolution provides an alternative by estimating patient‐specific AIFs directly from tissue data, up to a scale factor. This study compared blindly estimated AIFs with carefully measured aortic AIFs in breast DCE‐MRI.

title: Suprahyoid Muscle Activity and Fatigue During Tongue Elevation Compared With the Head Lift Exercise: A Surface EMG Study
creator: Tomoki Nanto, Yuta Nakao, Kazuki Eimoto, Yuki Oshima, Shigeo One, Rumiko Maeda, Shumpei Aizawa, Yuka Suetsugi, Takahiro Ono
description: BackgroundStrengthening the suprahyoid muscles is fundamental for effective swallowing rehabilitation. Although the head lift exercise is widely employed, it can prove challenging for certain patients. Tongue elevation against the hard palate has been proposed as a feasible alternative. However, its fatigue profile remains underexplored.

title: Association between thyroid feedback quantile‐based index and the risk of in‐hospital amputation in patients with diabetic foot ulcer
creator: Jiale Wang, Yujie Huang, Funeng Wang, Meiling Lao, Lijun Lan, Peiling Liang
description: AimsTo investigate the relationship between the thyroid feedback quantile‐based index (TFQI) and the risk of amputation during hospitalization in patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFU).MethodsThis single‐center retrospective study included 381 hospitalized patients with DFU and normal thyroid function. Logistic regression assessed continuous TFQI and quartiles.

title: Metandienone abuse induces hepatotoxicity via dysregulated inflammation and metabolic dysfunction
creator: Yangyang Ye, Jing Li, Zuodong Chen, Xiaoming Xue, Jinzhong Xi
description: ObjectiveTo explore the effects and mechanisms of metandienone abuse on hepatotoxicity.MethodsHepG2 cells were treated with 1 μg/mL metandienone for 24 h. Cell viability and apoptosis were detected via Cell Counting Kit-8 and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling assays, respectively. Cellular morphology was assessed via transmission electron microscopy. Genetic changes were analyzed using transcriptome sequencing. Meanwhile, metandienone (0.

title: Standardization of the Monocyte Monolayer Assay: Lessons Learned From Laboratory Optimization and Literature Review
creator: Shamee Shastry, Kavya Babu, Deepika Chenna, Ganesh Mohan, Kartik Iyer
description: ObjectivesSeveral variables influence the outcome of cellular assays. We conducted a comprehensive literature review to identify the factors affecting the Monocyte Monolayer Assay (MMA) and subsequently standardized the assay through systematic in‐house laboratory trials.MethodsThe study was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 involved a literature review using PubMed and Scopus databases to identify factors influencing the assay.

title: Correction: MRC1 and LYVE1 expressing macrophages in vascular beds of GNAQ p.R183Q driven capillary malformations in Sturge Weber syndrome
creator: Sana Nasim, Colette Bichsel, Stephen Dayneka, Robert Mannix, Annegret Holm, Mathew Vivero, Sanda Alexandrescu, Anna Pinto, Arin K Greene, Donald E Ingber, Joyce Bischoff
description: cted in the original publication. For completeness and transparency, both correct and incorrect versions are displayed below. Incorrect Fig. 6 EC-R183Q promote significant THP1 cell adhesion under static and laminar flow-induced condition. a Fluorescence-labeled THP1 cells were incubated with EC-WT and EC-R183Q under static conditions (N = 10). Adherent cells were quantified after 1 h.

title: From simulation to stimulation: a predictive synergy-based control strategy for functional electrical stimulation cycling in a person with spinal cord injury
creator: Alexandre B. Peres, Gabriel G. Carmona, Ana Carolina C. de Sousa, Roberto S Baptista
description: BackgroundFunctional electrical stimulation (FES) cycling stimulation strategies are often derived from heuristics, or able-bodied kinematics and electromyography, which may be unsafe and non-representative for people with complete spinal cord injury. Optimally controlled predictive musculoskeletal simulations with synergy implementation offer a way to generate individualized, physiologically plausible muscle trajectories without prior experimental data.

title: Clinically relevant genomic and phenotypic differences in virulence, antimicrobial resistance, and biofilm-associated tolerance between Streptococcus suis lineages ST1 and ST123
creator: Cristina Uruén, Clara M Marín, Luis Daniel González-Vázquez, Marcelo Gottschalk, Miguel Arenas, Jesús Arenas
description: Streptococcus suis is a Gram-positive bacterium and an important pathogen in pigs and humans. It can be classified into more than 3000 sequence types (STs), among which the ST1 and ST123 lineages are highly prevalent in Spain. ST1 is a globally distributed lineage, while ST123 has emerged within the last decade only in Spain.

title: Altered brain function and its spatial correlations with neurotransmitter maps in anterior shoulder pain patients
creator: Zhijun Diao, Huan Li, Yujia Li, Chengxiang Liu, Yunsong Zheng, Jingdong Lu, Yintao Liu, Zi Wei, Peng Liu, Haifa Qiao
description: Neuroimaging studies have reported that chronic pain may be associated with brain functional changes and related molecular mechanisms. However, there are few studies in anterior shoulder pain (ASP). Thus, we aimed to assess the possible brain functional changes and their associations with neurotransmitter receptor maps in ASP patients.

title: Rethinking EDSS-based ambulation assessment in multiple sclerosis using continuous variable monitoring
creator: Noah M. Werner, Melanie Schuette, Ramona Hagler, Jan Voth, Balázs Danajka, Patricia Kirschner, Markus Heibel, Tjalf Ziemssen, Uwe K. Zettl, Sven G. Meuth, Marc Pawlitzki, Lars Masanneck
description: BackgroundMultiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the central nervous system (CNS) characterized by relapses and progressive disability. The Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS), used to quantify disability, is based on single, discretely assessed and potentially inaccurate patient-estimated walking ability, whereas digital health technologies (DHTs) enable continuous activity monitoring and more objective assessment of real-world functional performance.

title: ASIC1a as an integrating node in ischemic neurotoxicity: crosstalk with NMDAR and TRPM signaling
creator: Ke Lai, Lu-Yang Wang
description: Ischemic stroke triggers acidosis, glutamate excitotoxicity and oxidative stress, which converge to disturb ionic homeostasis through several cation channels, including acid-sensing ion channel 1a (ASIC1a), N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDARs) and transient receptor potential melastatin (TRPM) channels. Emerging evidence suggests that ASIC1a functions as a context-dependent integrating node: protons directly gate ASIC1a, glutamate and bilirubin-associated signaling can modulate ASIC1a-dependent injury pathways.

title: Autochthonous dengue transmission in Europe: epidemiology, mechanisms, and modelling insights
creator: Giulia Campinopoli, Antonino Di Caro, Alessandra D’Alise, Francesco Conventi, Timothy D. McHugh, Gerry Melino, Alimuddin Zumla, Giuseppe Ippolito
description: BackgroundDengue is the most rapidly expanding arboviral infection globally, with rising incidence and widening geographic distribution driven by urbanisation, climate change, vector expansion, and global mobility. Although traditionally confined to tropical and subtropical regions, dengue is increasingly emerging in temperate settings, including Europe.

title: Organization of the first national workshop for families in Switzerland concerned with hereditary cancer syndromes
creator: Sarah Glick, Monica Aceti, Claire M Barton, Bettina M Zimmermann, Lisa Schiess, Muriel Fluri, Andrea Kaiser-Grolimund, Carla Pedrazzani, Elissa Azzi, Arianna Maria Elena Bonfanti, Barbara Peters, Benjamin Thiele, Pierre O Chappuis, Maria Caiata-Zufferey, Maria C Katapodi, The CASCADE Consortium
description: BackgroundAlthough Patient and Public Involvement (PPI) workshops with families affected by hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes can benefit both affected individuals and their support networks, PPI workshops are rarely being organized. This article presents the planning and implementation of a one-day PPI workshop for families affected by Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer (HBOC) or Lynch Syndrome (LS) in Switzerland.

title: Multimodal algorithmic fusion model for physical education assessment: spatiotemporal comparison of inertial measurement units and traditional scales
creator: Junlin Cheng, Zhen Li
description: BackgroundConventional physical education assessment depends on subjective teacher observation and simple rating scales, often resulting in subjective bias, low evaluation efficiency, and delayed instructional feedback.MethodsThis study constructed a hierarchical multimodal fusion framework integrating inertial measurement unit (IMU) data and expert rubric scores for standardized PE skill evaluation.

title: Matrix metalloproteinase-guided targeting of vesicular stomatitis virus to tumors following systemic administration
creator: Eileen Victoria Theune, William C. Theune, Elham Ahmadi, Conner C. Chiari, Neha Singh, Rory Geyer, Jason Tonne, Muriel Metko, Olamide T. Olaoba, Isabella China Wang, Dylan Dai, Jianbin Ruan, Robert Clark, Guangfu Li, Penghua Wang, Evan R. Jellison, Anthony T. Vella, Richard Vile, Kepeng Wang
description: The lack of tumor-specific targeting by oncolytic viruses (OVs) restricts their therapeutic potential. Here, we report a “cap-linker” strategy to modify the vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) glycoprotein (G protein, VSV-GIN). The modified VSV (Pro-VSVIN) loses its ability to infect cells until present in the tumor microenvironment, where the linker is cleaved by tumor-enriched matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs).

title: Comorbidity of borderline with antisocial and narcissistic personality disorders: a multimethod study
creator: Banafsheh Mohajerin, Parham Mohammadi, Richard Howard
description: BackgroundThe construct of borderline personality disorder (BPD) remains contentious, with some arguing that it embraces too much pathology to be of any real value as a clinical diagnosis. Examining BPD’s comorbidity is key to understanding its heterogeneous vs. homogeneous nature.

title: A systematic review of nature-based solutions for climate action in African cities
creator: Nicola Frances Rule, Cameron T McLean, Andrew Emmanuel Okem, Promise M Nduku, Johannes Bhanye, Collins Matiza, Fred Sato, Chipo Perseverance Mungenge, Onyekachi Esther Ogunniyi, Ignacio Pita-Vaca, Cherié Janine Forbes, Petra Holden, Christopher H Trisos, Debra C Roberts, Nicholas P Simpson
description: Nature-based solutions (NbS), including ecosystem-based adaptation, are increasingly proposed for climate action in African cities, but the evidence base is fragmented and lacks systematic synthesis of what is being implemented, where, and how effectively. We analysed 112 studies retained from a systematic review, covering 134 urban areas across 42 countries and including 45 informal settlements.

title: m6A-modified ATF4 regulates glucose/lipid metabolism via the Sestrin2/GSK3β axis to alleviate myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury
creator: Jie Wu, Jian Tong, Fen Zhang, Xingxing Li, Xizhi Liu, Yang Dong
description: BackgroundMyocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is a critical complication in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases, and its pathogenesis is closely associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and the imbalance of glucose/lipid metabolism. This study aims to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying glucose/lipid metabolism in MIRI and identify potential therapeutic targets.

title: Depth-dependent soil water-salt relationships in the Hetao Irrigation District, arid Northwest China: Implications for sustainable management
creator: Yuanqing Cao, Huihui Wang, Xuan Chen, Li Zhu, Debasis Mitra, Jianhong Zhou, Jianhong Zhou
description: Soil salinization threatens agricultural productivity in arid gravity irrigation systems worldwide, yet the depth-stratified relationships between soil water and salt content remain poorly characterized. We monitored soil moisture and electrical conductivity (EC) at six depths (0–100 cm) across 15 sites in the Hetao Irrigation District, China, during the 2025 growing season. Our results indicate a depth-dependent divergence in water–salt associations.

title: Benchmarking Q40 sequencing for sensitive and efficient detection of rare genomic variants
creator: Shumeng Duan, Yaqing Liu, Xiaorou Guo, Zhiyin An, Ruiwen Ma, Qiaochu Chen, Yanming Xie, Qingwang Chen, Ying Yu, Lianhua Dong, Leming Shi, Yuanting Zheng
description: BackgroundPhred quality score (Q score) is critical for sequencing accuracy, yet the impact of Q40-achieving sequencing technologies (99.99% accuracy) on detecting subtle biological variations remains unvalidated.ResultsUsing a comprehensive set of well-established DNA/RNA reference materials (Quartet, NIST-RM8398, SEQC2-HCC1395/BL, MAQC, and ERCC), we benchmarked Q40 sequencing (Element AVITI) against the conventional Q30 standard (Illumina NovaSeq 6000).

title: Left main ostium dissection due to the ATAAD with coronary malperfusion
creator: Vitalii Kravchenko, Oleh Sarhosh, Mykhailo Ishchenko
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionAcute aortic dissection is a life-threatening condition associated with extremely high mortality. The presence of malperfusion in this patient cohort significantly increases mortality, with coronary malperfusion being among the most critical and dangerous forms. Despite the existing consensus on the management of Neri type A and type C coronary ostial dissections, the optimal treatment strategy for Neri type B dissections remains controversial, with advocates of immediate coronary artery bypass grafting as well as proponents of coronary ostial repair.

title: Grade-specific associations between insomnia and depressive symptoms in adolescents: a cross-lagged panel network analysis
creator: Qian Chen, Si-Yang Liu, Shi-Hao Ma, Xiao-Song Shen, Wan-Jun Cheng, Gu-Bing Wang, Zong-Kui Zhou
description: BackgroundInsomnia and depression frequently co-occur during adolescence, posing significant challenges to adolescent mental health. However, the direction of their association remains inconsistent in the literature and may show grade-specific patterns. Grounded in psychopathology network theory and informed by the developmental psychopathology perspective, this study examined symptom-level associations between insomnia and depression to better characterize these association patterns.

title: Optimization of solid-state fermentation process of diets and its effects on growth performance and intestinal function in growing pigs
creator: Mengting Ji, Jingchao Liu, Qinglin Wang, Tianye Gong, Jiaqi Zhang, Meng Li, Xiaohong Guo, Yang Yang, Bugao Li
description: BackgroundBiological fermentation can improve animal growth performance and meat quality by optimizing feed nutritional properties. However, the complex fermentation parameters require further systematic optimization. This study aimed to establish and optimize a solid-state fermentation (SSF) process, evaluate changes in the feed microbial community and flavor metabolites, and investigate their effects on muscle development and intestinal barrier function in growing pigs.

title: Inhalation exposure to surrogate military burn pit emissions impairs systemic microvascular function: linking pulmonary insult and diverse peripheral responses
creator: Van Nguyen, Anand Ranpara, William T Goldsmith, Thomas P Batchelor, Jacob Hoyer, Howard D Leonard, Atefeh Razazan, Sara E Lewis, Jacob Krafcheck, Robert Burns, Randy J Nelson, Pallavi Sharma, James C Walton, Neeharika Beru, William Bain, Charles Dela Cruz, Mark Wilson, Eric E Kelley, Salik Hussain,
description: Millions of U.S. troops and supporting personnel have been deployed to military bases in the Middle East. Essentially all personnel on military bases were exposed to the combustion emissions generated by open pit waste burning. Chronic multisymptom illness (CMI) is a term advanced to characterize the complex health effects of inhalation exposures to military burn pits (BP).

title: Transferrin receptor 1: an emerging therapeutic target in cancer beyond iron metabolism
creator: Xuefei Fu, Yuan Feng, Zhendong Wu, Yunpeng Qin, Huan Qin, Kai Yao
description: Iron is an indispensable trace element for maintaining normal physiological functions in the body, participating in key biological processes such as energy metabolism, DNA synthesis, and damage repair. Under normal physiological conditions, cells tightly regulate iron homeostasis to prevent iron overload-induced oxidative stress and DNA damage.

title: The cGAS–STING pathway contributes to cisplatin-induced skeletal muscle atrophy through altered proteostasis and myogenic signaling
creator: Xiaoguang Liu, Miaomiao Xu, Huan Wang, Haozhe Wang, Hao Wang, Wenjun Fang, Mengqian Li, Jiongxing Huang, Feipeng Chen, Huiguo Wang, Yang Yu, Lin Zhu
description: BackgroundCisplatin chemotherapy is widely used for cancer treatment but frequently induces skeletal muscle atrophy, which compromises physical function and patient outcomes. The molecular mechanisms underlying this process remain incompletely understood. The cyclic GMP–AMP synthase–stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS–STING) signaling pathway, classically involved in innate immune responses, has recently been implicated in cellular stress and tissue dysfunction.

title: Emotional and sleep problems and their associated factors among specialized operation personnel on surface vessels
creator: Guorui Liu, Yanfei Zhang
description: ObjectiveTo investigate the prevalence of anxiety, depression, and sleep problems among specialized operation personnel on surface vessels, and to analyze their influencing factors.MethodsA total of 600 participants were randomly selected. Basic demographic and occupational information was collected using a general information questionnaire.

title: Prevalence of asymptomatic malaria and its associated factors in the Al Zuhrah district, Al-Hodeidah Government, Yemen, 2022
creator: Mohammed Ahamed Hajjam, Mohammed Abdullah Al Amad, Samar Saeed Nasher
description: BackgroundAsymptomatic malaria represents a significant health issue, especially in endemic regions where asymptomatic individuals serve as reservoirs. In Yemen, the Al-Hodeidah governorate is the primary endemic area. This study aims to determine the prevalence of asymptomatic malaria and its associated factors in Al-Zuhra District, Al-Hodeidah Governorate.

title: Development and validation of the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) questionnaire on pediatric pain management for physicians and nurses
creator: Qiao Shen, Xiaoqiong Wei, Wei Liu, Wenni Zhang, Hongyao Leng, Xianlan Zheng
description: BackgroundEffective pediatric pain management is often hindered by gaps in medical staff’s knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Few reliable instruments comprehensively measure these domains. This study aimed to develop and preliminarily validate a Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) Questionnaire on pediatric pain management for physicians and nurses.

title: In vitro study of TSC1 deficiency in preadipocytes: insights into development and treatment options for tuberous sclerosis related lipomatosis
creator: Julika E Friedrich, Julia Hentschel, Sandy Richter, Henriette Kiep, Maria Arélin, Konrad Platzer, Torsten Schulz, Andreas Merkenschlager, Wieland Kiess, Steffi Mayer, Rami Abou Jamra, Diana Le Duc, Antje Garten, Anna S Kirstein
description: BackgroundTuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a rare genetic neurocutaneous disorder resulting from mutations in the TSC1 or TSC2 genes, characterized by overgrowth and lesions in multiple organs. While renal angiomyolipomas are commonly seen, lipomas located elsewhere are rarely reported in these patients.

title: First aid educational needs among nursing officers in military primary clinics: a mixed-methods study
creator: Seoyoung Baek, Jiyeon Lee, Yungyong Jeon, Mi-So Shim, Chang Gi Park, Gwang Suk Kim
description: BackgroundEvidence regarding the first aid duties and educational needs of nursing officers in military primary healthcare facilities is limited. We aimed to develop a comprehensive first aid task inventory for nursing officers in such primary military clinics and to identify educational priorities using multiple analytic approaches.MethodsA cross-sectional mixed-methods design was employed.

title: Facility-level determinants of infection prevention and control monitoring in Somalia: evidence from the 2024 Harmonized Health Facility Assessment
creator: Abdikarim Abdi Adam, Mohamed Hassan Mohamed, Nor Haji Osman, Felix Emeka Anyiam, Kassim Abdi Jimale, Yahye Sheikh Abdulle Hassan, Shafie Abdulkadir Hassan
description: BackgroundSomalia lacks empirical data on routine infection prevention and control (IPC) monitoring at the health-facility level, despite ongoing gaps in IPC worldwide. Reducing healthcare-associated infections, preventing antibiotic resistance, and safeguarding healthcare personnel, especially in fragile health systems, all depend on effective IPC systems.

title: Dysmenorrhea patients’ experience with work productivity impact and treatment in Japan
creator: Osamu Hiraike, Daisuke Goto, Masahiko Uchiyama, Shoko Takahashi, Yutaka Osuga
description: BackgroundNearly 50% of Japanese women report impaired work performance due to menstrual symptoms. Our objectives were to describe the real-world experiences of patients living with dysmenorrhea with a focus on work productivity and its association with treatments. Our exploratory objective was to understand the coping methods for menstrual pain in Japanese women.

title: Aortic arch surgery in real-life practice: is the frozen elephant trunk always a better option than conventional aortic arch replacement?
creator: Maxime Zimmermann, Matteo Pozzi, Fadi Farhat, Marco Vola, Jean-François Obadia, Antoine Millon, Daniel Grinberg
description: ObjectiveManagement of aortic arch disease (AAD) is complex due to its involvement in multiple aortic segments and the variety of patient presentations. We compared the clinical outcomes of conventional aortic arch repair (CAAR) and the Frozen Elephant Trunk (FET) technique across the main clinical indications: acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), chronic dissection and atheromatous aneurysm.

title: Association between acupuncture exposure and mortality in people with disabilities diagnosed with ischemic heart disease: a nationwide retrospective cohort study in the Republic of Korea
creator: Hyungsun Jun, Jae-Uk Sul, Moon Joo Cheong, Hae‑Rim Kim, Inae Youn, Ye-Seul Lee, Jungtae Leem
description: BackgroundPeople with disabilities (PWDs) have higher incidence and mortality rates of cardiovascular disease than non-PWDs. Considering the mutual influence of cardiovascular diseases and disabilities, careful observation and complementary management beyond standard treatments are essential when ischemic heart disease (IHD) occurs in PWDs. This study investigated the association between acupuncture treatment and reduced mortality in PWDs diagnosed with IHD.

title: Pandemic to endemic: a longitudinal multinational study on COVID-19’s effects on graduate medical education
creator: Fatima Msheik-El Khoury, Jolene Ee Ling Oon, Lorraine Lewis, Halah Ibrahim, Sophia Archuleta
description: BackgroundThis study applied a resilience engineering framework to understand how international graduate medical educations (GME) programs responded to the disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Beyond describing early pandemic disruptions, we offer a multi-year, multi-country analysis of how training functions adapted, which elements durably changed, and what program design features may be associated with recovery.

title: Gender differences in early functional recovery after minimally invasive distal transverse metatarsal osteotomy - Akin Osteotomy (MITA) for hallux valgus: a propensity-matched study of 300 cases
creator: Taebyeong Kang, Jeong Hwan Lee, Dongoh Lee, Kyung Jin Choi, Sang Gyo Seo
description: BackgroundEvidence regarding sex-based differences in outcomes after minimally invasive distal transverse metatarsal osteotomy - Akin osteotomy (MITA) for hallux valgus remains limited. This study compared clinical and radiographic outcomes and complication rates between male and female feet using a propensity score–matched cohort.MethodsThis retrospective study included 300 feet (150 male and 150 female) that underwent MITA.

title: Hepatitis A virus seroprevalence and acute infection: a five-year retrospective analysis from central part of Turkey
creator: Burak Ezer, Rifat Bülbül
description: BackgroundHepatitis A virus (HAV) remains an important cause of acute viral hepatitis worldwide, with its epidemiology shifting in countries undergoing socioeconomic development. In Turkey, improvements in sanitation and the introduction of routine childhood vaccination in 2012 have reduced early-life exposure, potentially creating a susceptible population among adolescents and young adults.

title: Impact of community mental health center follow-up on psychiatric hospitalization burden in schizophrenia spectrum disorders: a retrospective mirror-image study
creator: Haluk Usta, İzgi Ayçıl Gencan Yilmazer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCommunity-based psychiatric rehabilitation services are increasingly used to reduce recurrent hospitalization and improve continuity of care among individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders. However, long-term real-world longitudinal data evaluating hospitalization outcomes following community mental health center follow-up remain limited.

title: Catheter-assisted evacuation through limited laminectomy for traumatic long-segment spinal epidural hematoma in ankylosing spondylitis: a technical note and two case reports
creator: Jie Shang, Bao Jia, MUSTAFA ABBAS FARHOOD SULTANI, Lei Liu, Jianwei Zhang, Jie Chen, Xianyi Zhang, Liang Guo, Peipei Li, Meng Han
description: BackgroundPatients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS) are prone to unstable spinal fractures with long-segment spinal epidural hematoma (LSEH). Conventional multilevel laminectomy can achieve complete decompression but may disrupt the posterior tension complex. In this article, we describe a catheter-assisted technique for evacuating LSEH through a limited laminectomy window.

title: Clinical efficacy and safety of interventional embolization combined with early rehabilitation in the management of post-traumatic shoulder periarthritis
creator: Biaorui Su, Yajun Hong, Zhenyu Li, Shandan Ouyang, Cong Yu, Fangming Geng, Jia Niu, Jin Peng
description: BackgroundPatients with refractory post-traumatic shoulder periarthritis(PTSP) have markedly reduced quality of life owing to persistent pain and functional restrictions. Thus, exploring a safe, effective treatment regimen is essential.AimThis study compared the efficacy and safety of TAE plus early rehabilitation versus rehabilitation alone for conservatively refractory post-traumatic shoulder periarthritis.

title: Comparison of 5.0T and 3.0T time-of-flight MR angiography for visualizing the anterior choroidal artery
creator: Zhangzhu Li, Mingyan Shang, Min Fu, Zhensong Wang, Liang Yin, Dan Yu, Jie Gan
description: BackgroundThis study aimed to compare the image quality of 5.0T and 3.0T time-of-flight (TOF) magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) for visualization of the anterior choroidal artery (AChA).MethodsThis retrospective study included patients who underwent both 3.0T and 5.0T TOF-MRA within a 48-hour interval. Objective image quality was assessed using signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR).

title: Photon-counting CT for paraspinal muscle fat quantification compared with MRI proton density fat fraction
creator: Dingbo Shu, Jianping Wang, Ding Liang, Li Zhao, Zhenhua Zhao
description: BackgroundTo evaluate photon-counting CT (PCCT) derived 70 keV attenuation values and virtual noncontrast fat fraction (VNC FF) in quantifying paraspinal muscle fat infiltration, using MRI proton density fat fraction (PDFF) as the reference standard.MethodsIn this prospective study, 76 adults with low back pain underwent same-day lumbar PCCT and 6-echo q-Dixon MRI within a 2-hour interval.

title: Clinical manifestations and laboratory findings in patients coinfected with dengue virus and SARS-CoV-2: a systematic review
creator: Rahadhyan Adnyanaschah, Rizky Abdulah, Monika Pury Oktora
description: BackgroundDengue Hemorrhagic Fever and Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) are infectious diseases caused by dengue virus (DENV) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). While DENV remains endemic in many tropical regions, SARS-CoV-2 spread globally beginning in 2020. Reports of coinfection have emerged from several countries.

title: Preoperative assessment of intratumor heterogeneity using intravoxel incoherent motion MRI for survival prediction in high-grade gliomas: a feasibility study
creator: Xingrui Wang, Yuanzheng Wang, Xiaoqing Wang, Fang Liu, Shiteng Suo, Yang Song, Yan Zhou, Mengqiu Cao
description: BackgroundIntratumor heterogeneity (ITH) is closely associated with poor prognosis in high-grade gliomas (HGGs). This study aimed to characterize ITH and explore potential imaging markers that predict overall survival (OS) in HGGs using intravoxel incoherent motion magnetic resonance imaging (IVIM MRI)-based spatially explicit analysis.MethodsSixty-five HGG patients who underwent surgical resection were analyzed.

title: Melatonin activates the ZjERF34-ZjMYB1 regulatory pathway to promote flavonoid biosynthesis and salt tolerance in jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.)
creator: Cuiping Wen, Zhongtang Wang, Chao Wang, Liguo Qiu, Haiyang Wang, Liying Xiao, Xingang Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundFlavonoids are essential secondary metabolites that contribute to fruit nutritional quality and stress adaptation. Jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) accumulates abundant flavonoids; however, the regulatory mechanisms by which melatonin (MT) modulates flavonoid biosynthesis remain poorly understood.ResultsIn this study, exogenous MT treatment markedly promoted flavonoid accumulation in jujube leaves and triggered dynamic changes in endogenous MT levels, implying a regulatory function of MT in this process. Transcriptomic and correlation analyses identified ZjMYB1 as a key MT-responsive regulator strongly associated with flavonoid accumulation.

title: Phytohormones producing endophytic fungi Paecilomyceslilacinus modulated metabolic, enzymatic, and non-enzymatic antioxidant systems of Zea mays L. under heavy metal stress
creator: Muhammad Musa, Rabia Khan, Imdad Ullah, Niaz Ali, Muhammad Fawad Khan, Misbah Bint Riaz
description: BackgroundThe continuous growth of the global population is intensifying the challenge of sustaining future food production. Among the major constraints to agricultural productivity, heavy metal (HM) contamination of soils has emerged as a serious environmental problem that adversely affects crop growth and yield. Environmentally friendly strategies are therefore needed to mitigate HM stress in plants.

title: Impact of residual cholesterol and inflammation risk on non-culprit plaque progression in patients with acute coronary syndrome: a serial optical coherence tomography study
creator: Dirui Zhang, Luping He, Boling Yi, Yishuo Xu, Chen Zhao, Ming Zeng, Yuhan Qin, Ziqian Weng, Ning Wang, Xue Feng, Lulu Li, Yini Wang, Jingbo Hou, Gary S Mintz, Sining Hu, Haibo Jia, Bo Yu
description: BackgroundAcute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) patients face recurrent cardiovascular events due to non-culprit plaque progression despite optimal secondary prevention, but the differential impacts of residual cholesterol risk (RCR, on-treatment LDL-C ≥ 1.8mmol/L) and residual inflammation risk (RIR, on-treatment hs-CRP ≥2 mg/L) on plaque microstructure dynamics remain undefined.

title: Parental hesitancy and refusal toward routine childhood vaccination after the COVID-19 vaccination period: a cross-sectional study
creator: Ozan Emre Eliaçık, Oğulcan Çöme, Tolga Günvar
description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic intensified public debates on vaccines, amplifying concerns about safety, side effects, rapid development, and institutional trust. These concerns may be associated with current attitudes toward routine childhood immunization. This study assessed parental intentions regarding routine childhood vaccination among parents whose children had previously completed routine immunizations.

title: Expression of Concern: Montenegro et al. Resveratrol-Loaded Lipid Nanocarriers: Correlation Between In Vitro Occlusion Factor and In Vivo Skin Hydrating Effect. Pharmaceutics 2017, 9, 58
creator: Pharmaceutics Editorial Office
description: Office and Editorial Board assessed the concerns and sought clarification from the authors. However, despite repeated attempts to obtain additional information, the concerns could not be conclusively resolved, because the Editorial Office was no longer able to establish contact with the authors.

title: CD4+T cells mediate systemic and local immune changes and pain symptoms in the rat model of temporomandibular disorders related pain
creator: Jianquan He, Yuzhuo Hei, Lin Li, Xiaojun Xia, Zhihui Mai, Xiayun Chen
description: Background and purposeImmune cells involved in pain has received increasing attention, but the available literature on the role of T cells in temporomandibular disorders (TMD) related pain is limited. Our previous study has showed that elevated expression of HLA DR+ CD4+ T cell may increase the risk of TMD-related pain.

title: FVRS: a cross-species multi-omics database for fruit and vegetable ripening and senescence
creator: Lili Ma, Yunxiang Wang, Yiting Ren, Caie Wu, Yuanye Jiang, Jiejie Tao, Xuelian He, Xinyi Feng, Tianyu Li, Xu Liu, Jingjing Jin, Jinhua Zuo, Yanyan Zheng
description: ause softening, colour change, off-flavour and nutrient decline, causing major food loss and economic costs (Giovannoni 2004), so understanding their regulatory networks is a core goal of postharvest biology. While high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometry have generated extensive multi-omics datasets (Guo et al. 2022; Ma et al. 2024; Tao et al.

title: Consistency of response to rimegepant for the acute treatment of migraine among real-world users – findings from the prospective observational CONFIDENCE study
creator: Richard B Lipton, Lucy Abraham, Alexandre Urani, Giorgio Lambru, Peter J Goadsby, Patricia Pozo-Rosich, Todd J Schwedt, Kristina M Fanning, Feng Dai, Karin Hygge Blakeman
description: BackgroundReal-world data on the effectiveness of rimegepant for the acute treatment of migraine is limited, particularly regarding consistency of response over multiple attacks.MethodsCONFIDENCE was a prospective observational survey study with screening and baseline questionnaires; a 28-day observational period where participants completed daily assessments on migraine occurrence, treatment, and outcomes; and an end of study questionnaire.

title: Public brain health: a framework for action to promote and safeguard brain health
creator: Timothy Daly, Dorothee Horstkötter, Harris Anthony Eyre, Emily Murphy, Seth Alan Gale, Lisa Cosgrove, Davide Bruno, Eoin Cotter, Andrea Slachevsky, James Rupert Fletcher, Lindsay Wallace, Abel Wajnerman-Paz, Jennifer Jaie Manly, Jonathan Fuller, Stella-Maria Paddick, Romain Manet, C. Elizabeth Shaab
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The promotion of brain health has generally been undertaken at the level of individuals, for instance, in the quest for precision treatments for persons with, or at high risk of, neurological disorders. But the growing global burden of neurological conditions and the increasing understanding of the brain’s central role in all facets of human life have spurred interest in public health approaches to the brain that emphasise population-level strategies benefitting everyone as part of a “brain health for all” vision of society.

title: PAGE: an R package for network detection of multivariate error-prone gene expression data with the availability of auxiliary information
creator: Li-Pang Chen, Wan-Yi Chang
description: BackgroundGene expression data in bioinformatics studies often contain multivariate or high-dimensional variables. One key research problem is to uncover the network structure among gene expression variables, which can help identify pathway-level disruptions associated with diseases and support the development of targeted therapies.

title: Children’s Cognitive Abilities Moderate Parent/Teacher Agreement on Internalizing and Externalizing Psychopathology
creator: Katherine All, Caden J. Carter, Melica Kemanian Leites, Rachel Wikander, Chaojian He, Cynthia L. Huang-Pollock
description: Multi-informant assessment (typically parents and teachers) is a gold-standard process used to inform diagnosis and tailor treatment in children, but multi-informant agreement is notoriously low. Children’s cognitive abilities might partially account for reporter discrepancies, particularly in situations when a child’s abilities are insufficient to meet context-specific demands (i.e.

title: Genome-wide identification of the SnRK gene family in willow and expression analysis under abiotic stress
creator: Hao Sun, Qianzhou Yuan, Jiaming Li, Min Ma, Haiyan Ren, Haifeng Song
description: BackgroundDrought and nitrogen (N) deposition significantly impact plant growth in northern regions. The balance between carbon (C) and N metabolism is crucial for plant adaptation to global environmental change. Salix gordejevii is widely distributed across the northern temperate zone and is characterized by rapid growth and high adaptability.

title: Anesthesia management for laparoscopic cholecystectomy and choledochoscopy-assisted intrahepatic bile duct stone extraction in a patient with situs inversus totalis, decompensated cirrhosis, and respiratory insufficiency: a case report
creator: Li Chen, Guoao Shi, Yihua Huang, Hengwei Sheng, Xu Dong, Li Kang
description: BackgroundSitus inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital anatomical anomaly characterized by mirror-image reversal of thoracic and abdominal organs. Perioperative management becomes particularly challenging when SIT coexists with inferior vena cava (IVC) malformation (e.g., agenesis of the hepatic segment), decompensated cirrhosis, and respiratory insufficiency—a complex scenario for which relevant anesthesia experience is exceedingly limited.

title: Real-world renoprotective effects of polyethylene glycol-loxenatide in type 2 diabetes: a multicenter, ambispective cohort study
creator: Junjun Ye, Jilin Li, Yongsong Chen, Fengwu Chen, Dan Zhu, Chuangyan Zhang, Qianyi Chen, Yu Tian, Shuhui Yang, Wencan Xu, Bin Xie, Zhe-Sheng Chen, Kaijian Hou
description: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease face persistent risks despite standard care. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide lacks real-world renoprotective evidence in high-risk Chinese populations relative to non-incretin-based standard care. This multicenter, ambispective cohort study enrolled 3305 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, renal impairment, and elevated cardiovascular risk at six Chinese tertiary institutions (median follow-up 36.

title: Development of a therapist-supervised flexibility and resistance exercise intervention for adults aged 50 years and over with a distal radius fracture in the Wrist Injury Strengthening Exercise (WISE) trial
creator: Warren Sheehan, Sarah E Lamb, Colin P Forde, Cynthia Srikesavan, Phillipa J A Nicolson, Elizabeth Tutton, Jenny Gould, Richard Grant, Juul Achten, Duncan Appelbe, Matthew L Costa, David J Keene
description: AimsThe definitive Wrist Injury Strengthening Exercise (WISE) trial is a multicentre superiority randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating usual care advice plus a therapist-supervised flexibility and resistance exercise intervention versus usual care advice alone for adults aged ≥ 50 years with a distal radius fracture (DRF).

title: Small‐scale adaptation to geothermal soil heating in a perennial herb revealed by combining crosses and transplantations
creator: Alicia Valdés, Vigdís F Helmutsdóttir, Bryndís Marteinsdóttir, Johan Ehrlén
description: Summary Identifying environmental factors associated with local adaptation and traits under selection is key to linking evolutionary processes to the environment. While reciprocal transplantation studies and provenance experiments often have demonstrated adaptation at relatively large spatial scales, adaptation can also occur at very small spatial scales.

title: Patient Preferences for Treatment Attributes in Moderate to Severe Chronic Hand Eczema: A Discrete Choice Experiment
creator: April W. Armstrong, Aseel Bin Sawad, Nisha C. Hazra, Sanjeev Balu, Douglas Maslin, Béa Libchaber, Rui Huang, Marjolaine Gauthier-Loiselle, Annie Guerin
description: IntroductionThe treatment landscape for Chronic Hand Eczema (CHE) is evolving; however, evidence on patients’ preferences regarding CHE treatment attributes is sparse. This discrete choice experiment (DCE) assessed how treatment attributes influence preferences among patients with moderate to severe CHE in the USA.MethodsAdults with moderate to severe CHE recruited from an online panel completed a web-based DCE survey (August–September 2025).

title: Topochemical synthesis of ternary metal sulfides including new LaAgS2
creator: Glen R. Hebberd, Toby J. Blundell, Leon Bowen, Stewart J. Clark, Emma E. McCabe
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ternary sulfides are increasingly sought after for applications as battery materials, photovoltaics and photocatalysts as a result of their small band gaps and good electrical conductivities but their synthesis is often more challenging than that of oxides. We report here the low temperature synthesis of new sulfide LaAgS2 by an anionic redox topochemical reaction, alongside the synthesis of LaCuS2 by mechanochemical topochemical reaction.

title: Early timepoint 99mTc-DPD whole body scintigraphy and quantitative SPECT/CT imaging for diagnosis of cardiac ATTR amyloidosis
creator: Stephan Settelmeier, Lukas Kessler, Noah Hammersen, Maria Papathanasiou, Christoph Rischpler, Alexander Carpinteiro, Sara Oubari, Lars Michel, Julia Vogel, Tim Wollenweber, Jing Ning, Marcus Hacker, Clemens P. Spielvogel, Zohreh Varasteh, Wolfgang P. Fendler, Francesco Barbato, Pedro Fragoso Costa,
description: BackgroundCardiac transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) is a progressive myocardial disease ultimately leading to heart failure. Standard diagnostic workup includes 99mTc-DPD scintigraphy performed after 2.5–3 h. The purpose of this study is to compare early (1 h after injection) to late imaging of 99mTc-DPD scintigraphy and SPECT for the detection of ATTR-CM. Early imaging could improve patient comfort and examination efficiency.

title: Efficacy Outcomes of Fecal Microbiota, Live-jslm in Preventing Recurrent Clostridioides difficile Infection from Seven Clinical Studies
creator: Teena Chopra, Daniel Van Handel, Brian Baggott, Robert Orenstein, Kelly Reveles, Beth Guthmueller, Shivam Srivastava, Sahil Khanna
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is one of the most common healthcare-associated infections in the US, and recurrence remains a major clinical challenge, as standard-of-care antibiotics fail to prevent recurrence in up to one-third of cases. Fecal microbiota, live-jslm (RBL) is the first single-dose, microbiota-based product approved by the US Food and Drug Administration and Health Canada for the prevention of recurrent CDI (rCDI) following standard-of-care antibiotics.

title: Ionic organic molecular cage-supported Pd nanoparticles for aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura coupling
creator: Brandon Bishop, Xiaoyu Fang, Simon Teat, Zhehao Yuan, Shuyan Jiang, Alec Kolodziejczyk, Qiucheng Xu, Wei Zhang
description: Spiroborate-linked organic molecular cages bearing bipyridine and phenanthroline ligands stabilize palladium nanoparticles whose dimensions are consistent with exocyclic growth. The cage-supported Pd nanoparticles act as efficient, recyclable catalysts for aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura coupling, affording high conversions under mild conditions while maintaining cage integrity, nanoparticle morphology, and activity over multiple cycles.

title: One-step generation of semi-cloned zebrafish carrying a defined genetic modification
creator: Yirui Ai, Shifeng Li, Siqi Liu, Jia Xu, Yunbin Zhang, Siyu Zhou, Zhou Zhou, Jinsong Li, Yiping Li
description: ations. In mice, androgenetic haESCs (AG-haESCs) carrying both H19-DMR and IG-DMR deletions can efficiently support the generation of semi-cloned pups upon intracytoplasmic AG-haESC injection (ICAHCI) into oocytes, at rates of up to 30.0% of transferred embryos. Therefore, mouse DKO-AG-haESCs have been used as a genetically tractable fertilization tool for complex genetic analyses at the organismal level.

title: Retraction: An epigenetic change in a moth is generated by temperature and transmitted to many subsequent generations mediated by RNA
creator: The
description: ta presented in the Reversed tab of S1 Data appear more repetitive than would be expected. Data presented in the Reversed tab of S1 Data appear more repetitive than would be expected. The article makes claims about epigenetic changes lasting 40 generations, but no data past the 12th generation are provided with the article.

title: Genome-scale metabolic modelling identifies vaginal microbiome members as potential probiotics
creator: Emma M. Glass, Glynis L. Kolling, Jason A. Papin
description: Probiotic supplements are marketed for diverse health benefits, yet species inclusion often lacks functional rationale. Our survey of 352 over-the-counter probiotic products available in the USA revealed 36 unique microbial species. However, there is no clear link between species inclusion and the intended health benefit.

title: PKPD-Based Translational Modeling of Calaspargase Pegol Preclinical Activity in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
creator: Eef Hoeben, Vincent Madelain, Chayan Acharya, Pierre Barbier Saint Hilaire, Ethika Tyagi, Malek Okour, Sylvain Fouliard
description: Background and ObjectiveCalaspargase pegol (CalPEG) is a PEGylated conjugate of L-Asparaginase (L-Asp) and an asparagine specific enzyme approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as a component of a multi-agent chemotherapeutic regimen for the treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) in children and young adults.

title: Incident Comorbid Diabetes and Outcomes in Multiple Sclerosis: An English Population‐Based Cohort Study
creator: Yolanda Lau, Sedigheh Zabihi, Morghan Hartmann, Georgina Mathlin, Sube Banerjee, Ebaa Marouf, Clare Hadley, Claudia Cooper, Ruth Dobson
description: ObjectiveTo compare the incidence of diabetes mellitus and its associations with hospitalisation and mortality in adults with multiple sclerosis (MS) and matched controls.MethodsUsing English primary care data from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink, linked to hospital and mortality records, we matched adults with MS with up to 10 controls without MS by age, sex and practice.

title: Multi-drug tolerance in Leishmania persister-like cells
creator: Allison Aroni-Soto, Pieter Monsieurs, Odin Goovaerts, Kaoutar Choukri, Basudha Khanal, Wim Adriaensen, Jean-Claude Dujardin, Michael P Barrett, Malgorzata A Domagalska
description: Leishmaniasis is caused by parasitic protozoa of the genus Leishmania and is found widely across the tropics and sub-tropics, afflicting hundreds of thousands of people. The disease is notoriously difficult to treat. Here, we present evidence of the existence of persister-like cells in cultured Leishmania populations, induced upon exposure to normally lethal doses of antimony, a still used anti-leishmanial.

title: RETRACTION: Recombinant Nanobody Against Muc1 Tandem Repeats Inhibits Growth, Invasion, Metastasis, and Vascularization of Spontaneous Mouse Mammary Tumors
creator: Unknown
description: RETRACTION: P. Merikhian, B. Darvishi, N. Jalili, M. R. Esmailinejad, A. S. Khatibi, S. M. Kalbolandi, M. Salehi, M. Mosayebzadeh, M. S. Barough, K. Majidzadeh‐A, F. Yadegari, F. Rahbarizadeh, and L. Farahmand, “Recombinant Nanobody Against Muc1 Tandem Repeats Inhibits Growth, Invasion, Metastasis, and Vascularization of Spontaneous Mouse Mammary Tumors,” Molecular Oncology 16, no. 2 (2022): 485‐507, https://doi.org/10.1002/1878‐0261.13123.

title: Environmental DNA from pumped deep-sea water enables monitoring of deep-sea fish diversity
creator: Takao Yoshida, Masaru Kawato, Shinji Tsuchida, Aya Yamazaki, Yoshihiro Fujiwara, Yuriko Nagano, Akinori Yabuki
description: Monitoring deep-sea biodiversity is challenging because conventional methods, such as net-sampling and visual surveys, require substantial logistical effort. Environmental DNA (eDNA) offers an alternative for detecting marine organisms; however, its application in deep-sea ecosystems is limited by the sampling accessibility.

title: Biobank-based genetic characterization of neurodegenerative diseases and idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus: insights and lessons learned from FinnGen
creator: Sami Heikkinen, Valtteri Julkunen, Henna Martiskainen, Mari Takalo, Eino Solje, Ville Leinonen, Annakaisa Haapasalo, Anssi Lipponen, Mikko Hiltunen
description: Brain disorders characterized by progressive neurodegeneration, such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD), represent an increasing medical and societal challenge. While genome‑wide studies have uncovered numerous susceptibility loci, these efforts have largely focused on common variants and leave a substantial portion of genetic liability unresolved.

title: Two-dimensional kinematic analysis of futsal instep shot performance in trained and novice players
creator: Xin Shen, Xiaomei Liu, Rahmat Hidayat, Yali Xu
description: This study provides a comparative kinematic analysis of futsal instep shot performance between trained athletes and novice players, addressing limited evidence on how multijoint kinematic patterns are associated with ball velocity. Twenty trained futsal athletes and twenty novice players performed standardized instep shots recorded using high-speed cameras at 240 fps.

title: Strong field spectroscopy of many-body interactions in solids
creator: Viacheslav Korolev, Thomas Lettau, Vipin Krishna, Alexander Croy, Martin Thümmler, Michael Zürch, Christian Spielmann, Maria Wächtler, Ulf Peschel, Stefanie Gräfe, Giancarlo Soavi, Daniil Kartashov
description: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron–hole polarization. Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved.

title: Keratin 18 functions as a lactyltransferase to trigger necroptosis in diabetic kidney disease by modulating Fas transcription
creator: Qiao Zhao, Xu Liu, Yangliang Yang, Fufen Meng, Zhipeng Meng, Minmin Zhu
description: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a type of chronic renal injury induced by diabetes mellitus and is characterized by persistent proteinuria and progressive decreases in the glomerular filtration rate. Recent studies have highlighted the significance of histone lactylation and necroptosis in the pathogenesis of DKD.

title: Mitophagy coordinates organelle crosstalk in health and diseases
creator: Mengyao Wu, Pengyi He, Yajun Lian, Tuo Zhang, Yiqi Wu, Lu Wang, Daolin Tang, Yongming Yao, Renqi Yao
description: Eukaryotic cells contain various membrane- and non-membrane-bound organelles, whose spatial and functional organization underpins intracellular homeostasis. Organelle coordination is governed by complex signaling and metabolic networks, often facilitated by direct physical contacts and molecular exchange. Mitochondria, as central hubs of bioenergetic and metabolic activity, are essential to functional coordination among cellular organelles.

title: Metabolomic signatures prior to in-hospital cardiac arrest: insights into potential therapeutic targets
creator: Taline Lazzarin, Julia S. Nunes, Raquel S. Ballarin, Paula S. Azevedo, Filipe W. L. Pereira, Sergio A. R. de Paiva, Suzana E. Tanni, Leonardo Zornoff, Rafael Garrett, Daryl Jones, Marina A. Alves, Marcos F. Minicucci
description: Plasma metabolomic alterations occurring up to 48 h before in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) and their associations with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and in-hospital mortality (IHM) were evaluated in this exploratory case-control study. Adults with IHCA at a tertiary university hospital were identified, and archived serum samples collected within 48 h before the event were analyzed.

title: Entinostat plus exemestane for hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer: long-term overall survival results from the EOC103A3101 randomized controlled trial
creator: Jiani Wang, Qingyuan Zhang, Xichun Hu, Tao Sun, Wei Li, Quchang Ouyang, Jingfen Wang, Zhongsheng Tong, Min Yan, Huiping Li, Xiaohua Zeng, Changping Shan, Xian Wang, Jian Zhang, Yue Zhang, Liang Zhang, Hongyan Shang, Binghe Xu
description: The addition of entinostat, a histone deacetylase inhibitor, to exemestane has demonstrated improved progression-free survival (PFS) in hormone receptor-positive (HR + ), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) advanced breast cancer (ABC) following endocrine therapy failure in the EOC103A3101 randomized trial (NCT03538171). This study reports long-term overall survival (OS) results.

title: Genetic and environmental influences on educational disparities in adult weight change: an individual-based pooled analysis of 11 twin cohorts
creator: Alvaro Obeso, Gabin Drouard, Aline Jelenkovic, Emanuela Medda, Corrado Fagnani, Virgilia Toccaceli, Antti Latvala, Sari Aaltonen, Sarah E. Medland, Scott D. Gordon, Jooyeon Lee, Soo Ji Lee, Joohon Sung, Hyojin Pyun, Glen E. Duncan, Dedra Buchwald, Juan R. Ordoñana, Juan F. Sánchez-Romera, Eduvigis C
description: IntroductionEducational attainment (EA) is negatively associated with body mass index (BMI), but less is known about the association between EA and adult BMI change. We analysed the role of genetic and environmental factors in the associations between EA and BMI trajectory components over adulthood.

title: Integrating machine learning and geospatial technologies for spatio-temporal analysis of urban expansion and land use transformation in Gambella Town, Ethiopia
creator: Kanenus Fufa Dararo, Goanar Jal Dup, Weyesa Merga Chemeda, Shankar Karuppannan
description: Rapid urbanization and the associated expansion of built-up areas are transforming land resources, ecosystem functions, and the spatial structure of cities. Distinguishing urban growth, urban expansion, and urban sprawl is essential for understanding the processes and patterns of urban transformation and supporting sustainable urban planning.

title: Conserved genetic and antigenic profiles of Pf12 and Pf41 in asymptomatic Plasmodium falciparum carriers in Tanzania
creator: Fadhila Fitriana, Wang-Jong Lee, Hyun-Young Sim, Hojong Jun, Jadidan Hada Syahada, Fauzi Muh, Se Jin Lee, Sunghun Na, Kyu Joon Lee, Joo-Won Nam, Eun-Taek Han, Jim Todd, Alphaxard Manjurano, Winifrida Kidima, Ernest Mazigo, Jin-Hee Han
description: Plasmodium falciparum remains a major cause of mortality in malaria-endemic regions, and strain-specific immunity limits vaccine efficacy. The 6-cysteine proteins Pf12 and Pf41 are proposed blood-stage vaccine candidates, yet their diversity and antigenicity in asymptomatic carriers are poorly defined. Genetic variation and natural selection pressure were analyzed in 172 P. falciparum isolates from asymptomatic individuals in Tanzania.

title: Retraction: Transcription Regulation of HYPK by Heat Shock Factor 1
creator: The
description: being used to represent different experimental conditions: The left and right Fig 2D AcH4 panels. The left and right Fig 2D AcH4 panels. The left Fig 2D RNA polymerase II panel in [1] and the Fig 2C RNA polymerase II panel in [2].

title: Seasonal and environmental patterns of naturally occurring parasitoids with potential to attack the invasive pest Drosophila suzukii in the Andes
creator: Déborah Fischbein, Mónica Daniela Germano, Andrés Santiago Martínez, Julian Mensch, Marcelo Eduardo Kun, Andrea Cardozo, Verónica Chillo
description: Landscape complexity shapes insect spatiotemporal population dynamics and trophic interactions. In this context, understanding seasonal and environmental patterns of potential resident natural enemies of novel polyphagous herbivores, such as the globally invasive fruit fly pest Drosophila suzukii, is fundamental for developing effective landscape-scale pest management strategies.

title: Increased temperature selects for antibiotic resistance genes in a model aquatic ecosystem
creator: Emma Bousquet, Sabine Favre-Bonté, Thibault Meyer, Concepción Sánchez-Cid
description: There is a rising concern that temperature increases associated with climate change might select for antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in aquatic ecosystems, although the extent of this phenomenon remains unknown. This study aimed to determine whether increased temperatures induce ARG selection and modify the transcriptional response in a model aquatic ecosystem using an omics approach.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid and dural accumulation of α-synuclein impairs CNS clearance in Parkinson’s disease
creator: Taylor J. Stevenson, Luca Vinnell, Samuel J.C. McCullough, Daniel X. Flyger, Blake Highet, James A. Wiseman, Ben Watkin, Kate Hitpass Romero, Victoria F. Low, Amy M. Smith, Angela Wu, Dahna M. Fong, Natasha L. Grimsey, Birger V. Dieriks, Clinton P. Turner, Deborah Young, Maurice A. Curtis, Richard L
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Impaired waste clearance and chronic inflammation are emerging contributors to Parkinson’s disease pathogenesis. Here, Stevenson et al. show that aggregated α-synuclein at CNS borders promotes TNF-driven meningeal inflammation and impairs CNS clearance, identifying these tissues as potential therapeutic targets. Introduction

The central nervous system (CNS) relies on specialized clearance pathways to remove metabolic waste and maintain neurological health (Kim et al., 2025; Kipnis et al., 2025; Rustenhoven and Kipnis, 2022).

title: Dynamic Changes in Serum Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein Levels Predicts Early Neurological Deterioration After Intravenous Thrombolysis in Minor Stroke
creator: Jie Zhou, Yang Qu, Reziya Abuduxukuer, Peng Zhang, Ting Wang, Jian‐Hua Gao, De‐Wang Pan, Zhi‐Mei Yuan, Chun‐Ying Li, Li‐Ping Chen, Jin‐Hua Chen, Ji‐Liang Gu, An‐Ying Wang, Li‐Gang Jiang, Liang Liu, Yong‐Fei Jiang, Chun‐Fei Wang, Yan Jia, Hong Xin, Chun‐Li Jiang, Ying‐Bin Qi, Xue‐Feng Hu, Song Li, Ha
description: ObjectiveMinor strokes may be associated with early neurological deterioration (END) and disabilities. The objective was to investigate the role of serum glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) levels in predicting END.MethodsData originated from a multicenter cohort study conducted prospectively. ΔGFAP was calculated as the ratio of post‐thrombolysis GFAP at 24 h to baseline GFAP.
